description:
Redwood Inference is seeing elevated p95/p99 latency during bursty traffic on several high-throughput chat/generation routes. Investigation points to KV cache behavior under load: fragmentation, long-lived allocations, and suboptimal eviction when the working set shifts quickly (e.g., spikes of long prompts followed by many short decodes). The project will add a KV cache compaction and eviction strategy in the serving runtime to reduce tail latency and stabilize throughput during bursts.

Goals:
- Reduce tail latency (p95/p99) during burst traffic without materially regressing steady-state throughput.
- Improve memory efficiency by reducing KV fragmentation and reclaiming unused KV blocks quickly.
- Add observability: metrics and traces that distinguish allocation pressure, fragmentation, compaction work, and eviction events.
- Ship safely: feature-flagged rollout with canarying, clear rollback, and updated oncall runbooks.

Scope:
- Runtime changes in the KV cache manager: tracking allocation/fragmentation, introducing a compaction mechanism (e.g., block relocation/defragmentation) and an eviction policy suitable for burst workloads (e.g., clock/LRU with cost-aware heuristics).
- Integration with scheduler/backpressure so compaction/eviction doesn’t amplify latency spikes.
- Performance suite updates to reproduce burst patterns and prevent regressions.
- Documentation: design spec + ADR, operational runbooks, release notes, and known-issues guidance.

Out of scope (initial iteration):
- Major changes to model kernels or attention implementations unrelated to cache management.
- Cross-region routing policy changes; those are handled separately by SRE/platform.

Stakeholders:
- Runtime engineering (primary): Mateo Alvarez (VP Eng, Runtime), Omar El-Sayed / Samir Qureshi (KV cache + memory), Sofia Ivanova’s team (scheduling integration).
- Applied ML / Perf & Evals: Jonas Weber’s org for benchmarking methodology and regression gates.
- SRE: Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes for canary, dashboards, and oncall procedures.
- Release Engineering: Connor O’Brien for release train coordination.
- Product (Dedicated): Lauren Bishop to ensure Dedicated burst/SLA messaging and rollout expectations.

Timeline (typical 4–6 weeks):
1) Week 1: Problem statement + design spec + ADR; define KPIs and test workloads.
2) Weeks 2–3: Implement compaction + eviction + metrics, plus correctness and stress tests.
3) Week 4: Perf suite scenarios, perf-canary gating, initial canary rollout.
4) Weeks 5–6: Gradual rollout, documentation updates, retro, and follow-ups.

Deliverables:
- Feature-flagged KV cache compaction/eviction in runtime.
- New metrics/dashboards and an updated profiling playbook.
- Benchmark artifacts demonstrating improved tail latency under burst patterns.
- Runbook + release notes + customer comms (if relevant to an escalation).

files.description: Primary design spec: problem statement, current KV cache behavior, proposed compaction algorithm, eviction policy, scheduler interaction, correctness considerations, and feature flag/rollout plan.
ADR capturing the chosen approach (e.g., compaction strategy + metadata format), alternatives considered, tradeoffs (latency vs overhead), and decision owners/approvers.
Updates performance standards: required metrics (fragmentation ratio, eviction rate, compaction time), how to report p99 under burst, and minimum acceptance thresholds for runtime releases.
Benchmark plan defining burst traffic scenarios, prompt-length distributions, concurrency ramps, and KPIs (p95/p99, OOM rate, throughput, GPU memory utilization).
Playbook: how to detect KV fragmentation and allocation pressure using traces/metrics; how to interpret compaction counters; step-by-step profiling workflow.
Oncall runbook for tail-latency events: toggling feature flags, adjusting cache limits, selecting eviction mode, and safe rollback steps.
Release notes entry describing the new compaction/eviction behavior, new flags, expected improvements, and any operational considerations.
Known issues/workarounds for initial rollout: edge cases, tuning guidance, and conditions where compaction may be disabled.
Retro covering what worked, what didn’t, rollout outcomes, and follow-up action items (tests, docs, guardrails).
Product-facing requirements note: how improvements impact Dedicated burst behavior, SLO expectations, and customer messaging/enablement.
GitHub issue: problem statement, incident links, baseline graphs, suspected root causes, and project checklist.
PR implementing KV cache compaction core (allocation bookkeeping, relocation/defrag logic), with unit tests and safety checks.
PR adding eviction policy implementation (e.g., clock/LRU hybrid), tuning parameters, and correctness tests.
PR adding runtime metrics and tracing spans: fragmentation gauge, compaction durations, eviction counters, allocation failure events.
PR adding burst-pattern benchmarks (ramps, mixed prompt lengths) and exporting comparable p95/p99 metrics.
PR introducing feature flag wiring, config defaults, and rollback guardrails (safe disable path, compatibility).
PR integrating new KPIs into perf-canary to block regressions in burst p99 and fragmentation-related failure modes.
PR updating runtime configuration docs and examples for new compaction/eviction flags and recommended settings.
Release artifact capturing changelog items, linked PRs, rollout notes, and any migration guidance.
Benchmark results report (tables/plots) comparing baseline vs compaction/eviction enabled across burst scenarios.
Follow-up issue to track long-term fragmentation regressions, add additional tests, and refine heuristics based on production telemetry.
Captured review discussion: concerns about overhead, correctness invariants, and chosen data structures for block metadata.
Linear epic: milestones and ownership across design, implementation, benchmarks, rollout, and docs.
Linear task: produce design spec + ADR, align with runtime scheduling and SRE rollout requirements.
Linear task: implement eviction policy + tuning parameters and validate correctness under mixed workloads.
Linear task: implement compaction mechanics, memory accounting, and safe pause/limits to avoid latency spikes.
Linear task: define metrics, update dashboards/alerts, add tracing annotations for oncall triage.
Linear task: add burst scenarios to perf suite, establish baselines, and publish results artifact.
Linear task: staged rollout plan, canary gates, rollback criteria, and coordination with Release Eng.
Linear task: retro, list of follow-ups, and ownership assignments for long-term hardening.
Slack thread with runtime engineers diagnosing burst p99 spikes, sharing graphs, and narrowing to fragmentation/eviction behavior.
Discussion of compaction approaches, overhead concerns, and how to bound compaction work per decode step.
Thread debating eviction policies (LRU/clock/segmented), fairness, and impact on long contexts under burst.
Architecture channel review: ADR feedback, required invariants, and sign-off notes.
SRE discussion: what to alert on (fragmentation vs allocation failures), thresholds, and noise control.
Incident channel log around a burst-latency event: mitigations applied, notes on cache pressure, and action items for runtime changes.
Release coordination thread: canary plan, feature flag defaults, and timeline for staged rollout.
Thread sharing benchmark numbers and plots; discussion of regressions, parameter tuning, and next test runs.
Thread aligning on metric names/labels to avoid high cardinality and ensure useful breakdowns.
Oncall channel notes about new mitigation knobs and how to use them during tail-latency pages.
Thread debating default enablement by model/region, safety rails, and gradual ramp strategy.
Platform/runtime scheduling discussion: how to budget compaction work vs request latency and when to defer compaction.
Thread discussing correctness edge cases (long contexts, prefill->decode transitions) and tests to add.
SRE checklist for go/no-go: canary KPIs, error budget impact, rollback criteria, and comms plan.
Thread summarizing remaining tasks, owners, and timelines (docs, benchmarks, follow-up issues).
Support channel thread: customer-reported symptoms, interim mitigation guidance, and escalation to runtime/SRE.
Postmortems channel discussion linking incident learnings to compaction rollout and monitoring improvements.
Internal announcement about rollout status, what changed, where to watch metrics, and how to report issues.
Meeting transcript/notes: baseline tail-latency evidence, design review, decision points, and action items.
Incident mitigation sync recording: timeline, immediate mitigations, and requirements for runtime compaction/eviction changes.

Support ticket capturing customer details, repro info, logs/graphs, and linkage to runtime issue/rollout status.
